title: Unified deployment contract spec and environment-aware capacity constraints
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a single machine-readable 'deployment contract' that captures the guarantees and constraints for a model release across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments. The contract is intended to be the authoritative source used by the rollout engine, admission controller, and runtime translators to: specify allowed model variants, minimum capacity and latency SLOs, routing fallbacks, KV-cache compatibility, quantization shape constraints, and per-environment feature gates (e.g., KMS usage, network egress restrictions). Goal: remove ad-hoc if/else logic across the stack and make environment-specific policies explicit and versionable.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable contract schema (v1) exists and is checked into rw-orchestration/specs/deployment_contract_v1.json
Rollout engine accepts a contract and enforces its admission constraints in a dev cluster (canary and shadow paths)
Runtime translator maps contract fields to concrete resources for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private without hard-coded environment switches
Automated test suite validates that a failing constraint (e.g., insufficient GPUs in Private) triggers policy-based auto-rollback or staged pause
Operational dashboard shows contract->deployment mapping and highlights violations with links to failing pods/hosts
implementation_notes: Design: contract is JSON Schema with top-level sections: metadata, constraints, allowed_variants, routing_policy, fallbacks, observability_requirements, security_requirements
Key constraints to represent: min_qps_per_instance, max_tokens_per_sec, allowed_quantization_modes, required_kms_profile, egress_rules, affinity_labels, allowed_gpu_families

Translator layer: implement translators/org-specific adapters that convert contract to concrete Kubernetes resources (Hosted->managed pools, Dedicated->reserved node pools, Private->customer node selectors and subnet annotations)
Admission controller: validates incoming rollout manifests against the bound contract; returns structured rejection reason used by rollout UI and can trigger automated rollback scripts

Sample contract snippet (human-readable, included in dev docs):
---
metadata:
  name: resnet-v2-nightly
  contract_version: v1
constraints:
  min_gpus: 2
  max_latency_ms: 120
  allowed_quant_modes: ["int8", "fp16"]
  require_kms: true
routing_policy:
  canary_ratio: 0.05
  shadow_enabled: true
fallbacks:
  - type: model_variant
    target: resnet-v2-qa
    condition: latency_above_200ms
---
Compatibility: include a 'capabilities' vector per environment so we can compute a compatibility score and automatically choose nearest variant with highest score
Edge-case: if Dedicated pool is constrained but Hosted has capacity, the routing policy can allow cross-environment spillover only for low-privacy models (flagged in contract)
decisions: Use JSON Schema v1 for contract definition to allow validation without custom parsers
Translator/adapters will live in rw-orchestration/adapters/ and be pluggable by environment type
Contracts are versioned and immutable once bound to a rollout; new rollouts require a new contract version
Security gates (KMS, VPC-only) are explicit booleans in contract; translators must fail fast if environment cannot satisfy them
risks: Overly strict contracts could block valid rollouts and cause availability regressions if resources are underprovisioned
If translator logic diverges, we reintroduce environment-specific behavior; need conformance tests
Private customers with air-gapped environments may require manual approval paths that delay automations
testing_plan: Unit: JSON Schema validation + translator unit tests for Hosted/Dedicated/Private adapters
Integration: deploy a canary with a failing constraint (min_gpus too high) and assert rollout is paused and an automated ticket is created
Chaos: simulate region outage and confirm fallback routing triggers model_variant fallback and triggers rollback if variants also fail
E2E: use the existing rollout-qa pipeline to exercise 0.05 canaries and shadow 100% traffic for a non-sensitive model; assert telemetry and log correlation
